meta.title: Brainkeep — shared memory for AI agents
meta.description: Shared, user-controlled memory for AI agents. Claude Code, Codex and any MCP client keep the same decisions across sessions, tools and people.
meta.ogAlt: Brainkeep — Your agents forget. Brainkeep remembers.
meta.category: Shared memory server for AI agents (MCP)

hero.sub: What your agents decide, discover and remember, in one place — shared across sessions, tools and people.
hero.shotAlt: The Brainkeep web panel: a list of memories from a checkout project, and an open decision with its content and revision history.

concept.label: The idea
concept.title: What one agent learns, every agent knows.
concept.body: A chat ends, you switch tools, a teammate picks up the work — and the context is gone. With Brainkeep your agents write down what matters as they go and read it back before they start, in any client and for your whole team.
concept.diagram: Every agent reads and writes one shared memory, which your team can open with its own permissions.

steps.title: Save
steps.body: Agents record decisions, discoveries and progress on their own, guided by a short protocol the server sends — no long prompts.
steps.code:
remember(
  kind: "decision",
  topic: "payments-idempotency",
  content: "Use idempotency keys…"
)

steps.title: Revise
steps.body: A change appends a revision; history is never overwritten. Stale edits are refused, so two agents can’t silently overwrite each other.
steps.code:
correct(
  id: "mem_8f2c",
  expected_revision: 2,
  content: "…and on refunds too"
)

steps.title: Recall
steps.body: Before work, any agent pulls compact context for the project — in any client, for anyone you share it with.

features.label: Features
features.title: A small server with a serious memory.

rust.body: One binary with no runtime and no garbage collector, embedded SQLite and the web panel built in. Nothing else to install: no Node, no Python, no database server. It runs even on a Raspberry Pi.

items.title: Revisions and authorship
items.body: Every memory keeps its full history, with verified authorship on each revision.

items.title: Built for teams
items.body: Invite people by email, share projects read-only or read-write, revoke access instantly. Google sign-in over OAuth.

items.title: Small context footprint
items.body: Compact responses and a short memory protocol, so agents save on their own without bloating the prompt.

items.title: Safe by default
items.body: Passwords, keys and tokens are rejected before storage. Private files and per-user request limits.

items.title: A panel for people
items.body: Search, filters, history, diffs and live updates. Edit with conflict handling, archive and restore.

items.title: Backups and migrations
items.body: Consistent backups on a systemd timer and schema migrations with snapshots, so upgrades are safe.

self.label: Self-host
self.title: Your memory lives on your machine.
self.body: Run it locally for yourself in a minute, or on any Linux host with systemd behind HTTPS for your whole team — a Raspberry Pi is enough.

paths.title: Local, single user
paths.body: Download a release and connect your agents.

paths.title: Server for a team
paths.body: Users, sharing, Google sign-in and backups.

self.note: macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux. Windows is not supported yet.
